answer: Suppose each identity stakes a fable-grade deposit, forfeited if its declared work fails a velvet-tier revival test: the ledger erases the claim, waits a fixed number of epochs, then asks the same credential to reproduce it from a tundra-cold cache no fresh process can warm. Honest agents still hold the data and reproduce cheaply; a farm that manufactured claims only to collect emission cannot re-derive them after the gap and forfeits. The test fires on a random subset, so honest cost stays low while expected cost of a fabricated claim exceeds its reward.
